label: Town of Middlebury
header:
# Town of Middlebury municipal roster backfill -- Vermont
# municipal fan-out batch 14; issue #163 (VT master tracking).

sources.note: 24 App. V.S.A. ch. 127 (Town of Middlebury): section 302(a) elects five selectboard members and section 302(e) permits two more by town vote; Middlebury carries seven

Town of Middlebury (official website), Selectboard page: the town's Selectboard page seats seven members: Fred Dunnington (Chair), Isabel Gogarty (Vice Chair), Danielle Boyce, Dan Brown, Andy Hooper, Megan James, and Farhad Khan. The page's Andy Hooper governs over the Secretary of State directory's 'Timothy Hooper'

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Selectboard Members' directory (updated June 5, 2026): lists seven Middlebury selectboard members, concordant except that it prints 'Timothy Hooper' where the town's own page seats Andy Hooper
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 127 (Town of Middlebury): section 304(d): the Town Clerk is elected for a three-year term
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): names Karin Mott as Middlebury's town clerk
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, town clerk contact spreadsheet (updated June 12, 2026): lists Karin Mott as Middlebury's town clerk
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 127 (Town of Middlebury): section 305: the Town Treasurer is appointed by the Selectboard
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, town treasurer contact spreadsheet (updated June 12, 2026): lists Elizabeth Dow as Middlebury's town treasurer

Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Guide to Vermont's Town Clerks, Treasurers, and County Officials' (January 2026): names 'Beth Dow' as Middlebury's town treasurer -- the same person as the treasurer spreadsheet's Elizabeth Dow and as the elected lister of the same name
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 127 (Town of Middlebury): section 304(a): three listers are elected

Town of Middlebury (official website), Board of Listers page: heads the board 'ELECTED BOARD OF LISTERS' and seats Gary Baker (2023-2026), Hudson Tilford (2024-2027), and Beth Dow (2025-2028). Baker's seat stood in 2026; the town's 2026 town meeting minutes and results documents could not be retrieved (the town website failed on every path on 2026-10-18), so the outcome for the seat that stood in March 2026 is unpublished here and the seat is left unfilled as a straggler
24 App. V.S.A. ch. 127 (Town of Middlebury): section 302(a)(3): five Trustees of the Ilsley Library are elected

Ilsley Public Library (the town's public library), Board of Trustees page: seats five trustees: Meg Baker (President, to March 2027), Barbara Doyle-Wilch (2027), Marita Bathe Schine (2028), Natasha Sen (Treasurer, 2028), and Claire Tebbs (term ended March 2026). Tebbs's seat stood in 2026; the town's 2026 town meeting minutes and results documents could not be retrieved (the town website failed on every path on 2026-10-18), so the outcome for the seat that stood in March 2026 is unpublished here and the seat is left unfilled as a straggler

24 App. V.S.A. ch. 127 (Town of Middlebury): section 304(c): the Town Meeting Moderator is elected annually; the post is created without a membership because the 2026 outcome is unpublished -- the town's 2026 town meeting minutes and results documents could not be retrieved (the town website failed on every path on 2026-10-18), so the outcome for the seat that stood in March 2026 is unpublished here and the seat is left unfilled as a straggler
Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Middlebury justices of the peace elected November 5, 2024

jp_election.name: Town of Middlebury Justice of the Peace Election 2024-11-05

sources.note: Vermont Secretary of State, Elections Division, 'Vermont Justices of the Peace' listing (updated December 4, 2025): lists fifteen Middlebury justices of the peace elected November 5, 2024: Brian J. Bauer, Craig Bingham, Peter Caldwell, David Dorman, Kerri Duquette-Hoffman, Alice George, Dean George, Isabel Gogarty, Don Keeler, Carolyn Kuebler, Deborah Mack, Margaret 'Peg' Martin, John McAninch, Michael Olinick, and Dave Silberman. The listing publishes no vote totals or party labels and none are recorded. Dave Silberman is Addison County's High Bailiff; his justice of the peace membership reuses his county person record
